pr_title: tests: mem_slab: Extend with CONFIG_MULTITHREADING=n case
pr_body:
Extended mslab_api test suite to support case when
multithreading is disabled.

Fixes #40020  

Signed-off-by: Lixin Guo <lixinx.guo@intel.com>
pr_comments: can be close due to merge of #40035

issue_context.title: tests: kernel: mem_slab: mslab_api: undefined reference to z_impl_k_sem_give and z_impl_k_sem_take
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Builds are failing in CI for `qemu_cortex_m0` and the test case `tests/kernel/mem_slab/mslab_api/kernel.memory_slabs.api_no_multithreading` because `k_sem_give()` and `k_sem_take()` have no implementation.

Seems to work fine on other platforms.

**To Reproduce**
```
twister -i -p qemu_cortex_m0 -s tests/kernel/mem_slab/mslab_api/kernel.memory_slabs.api_no_multithreading
```

**Expected behavior**
CI should be running smoothly.

**Impact**
Showstopper

**Logs and console output**
```
/opt/toolchains/zephyr-sdk-0.13.1/arm-zephyr-eabi/bin/../lib/gcc/arm-zephyr-eabi/10.3.0/../../../../arm-zephyr-eabi/bin/ld.bfd: app/libapp.a(test_mslab_api.c.obj): in function `k_sem_take':
/workdir/zephyr/twister-out/qemu_cortex_m0/tests/kernel/mem_slab/mslab_api/kernel.memory_slabs.api_no_multithreading/zephyr/include/generated/syscalls/kernel.h:1026: undefined reference to `z_impl_k_sem_take'
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: CI
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK v0.13.1
 - Commit: e8f09b471e

**Additional context**
https://buildkite.com/zephyr/zephyr/builds/45153

I have not narrowed down the exact commit that broke this test.
comments:
The root cause of this issue is one of the test cases in mslab_api test suite needs multithreading environment, but it is not supported by qemu_cortex_m0.
So in that test case, I excluded the case of single thread to make sure it only runs on multithreading platform.

review_comments: Would it be better if we put ztest_test_skip() here? It means test case is skipped, not pass.
Hi, @enjiamai , put ztest_test_skip() here will trigger a build error which is the same as #40020, so it's better to be a return here.
